resolution.note: backlog triage 2026-11-07: Handoff across Claude/Codex; same outcome

title: Make Herdr session handoff measurable, acknowledged and single-writer for Claude and Codex
body:
Outcome: one handoff mechanism owned in KRN (shared protocol + client adapter + repository adapter) so long work moves between Claude Code and Codex sessions in Herdr without losing goal, grants, evidence or single-writer control. Order: measurement and takeover correctness first, cost tuning second.
Source: operator handoff 2026-11-05, full report /home/krn/reports/Przekazywanie kontekstu w Herdr.md, notes /home/krn/research_notes/Przekazywanie kontekstu w Herdr/.
Confirmed defects (code + controlled repro, no observed data loss yet):
- global context-usage.py takes the last message.usage without provenance: a sidechain record replaced 210k with 11k; synthetic/partial usage gives 0 and should_relay=false. Missing data must be unknown, never 0; post-compaction samples are stale; worker usage never stands in for the main session. Claude occupancy = input + cache_creation + cache_read; Codex cached_input_tokens is a subset of input_tokens (do not add).
- global relay.sh waits a fixed 15 s and reads lifecycle; no proof the successor read the right handoff.
- scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts treats command success as start success and has the successor retire the predecessor before reading the handoff; retirement sweeps marked tabs across the whole workspace without checking project, outcome and unsent input (overlaps t-e6kke4g).
- Codex: no proven Codex->Codex relay; needs its own adapter (session telemetry or App Server thread/tokenUsage/updated), cross-client handoff tested separately (overlaps t-b6v615x, t-tdkpgag).
- Inherited HERDR pane ids can return pane_not_found; never fall back to the focused pane.
Protocol: checkpoint -> freeze predecessor writes -> durable handoff doc -> constrained successor start -> ACK of handoff id + hash -> atomic owner change (write generation) -> successor writes -> careful predecessor close. A timeout never proves a start did not happen: read the record before retrying. Single writer is cooperative until enforcement is found; a new hook needs a separate install/hook-trust grant.
Thresholds: keep 300k as reference; split prepare / no-new-large-work / execute thresholds; 150-180k is a hypothesis for a pilot on identical tasks.
Boundaries: no install/seal, production or hook trust without their grants; never close foreign, working or ambiguous panes; repos may hold others' uncommitted work.
Proof: tests for lost ACK, timeout after real start, two starters, crash before/after owner change, stale write grant, pane change, unsent input, dirty repo, active workers, compaction mid-work, on the real Herdr interface in an isolated workspace.
First slice: fix measurement (provenance, unknown/stale, per-client sum) with Claude receiver proof and an explicit Codex adapter scope; then successor ACK.

title: Deliver tracker-only PRs without commit contracts
body:
Observed defect (PR #160, 2026-11-01): krn deliver cannot deliver a tracker-only PR. Branch commit validation (src/flow/repository.ts, used by preflight and review) accepts only `<test file>:red->green|green->green` Change-contract trailers and refuses `none (...)`, while deliver's mergeMessage (src/deliver/message.ts:25) throws "PR commits require Change-contract trailers" when no commit carries one. The lead had to replay deliver by hand: publish krn/judge-* statuses, run the host-locked gate, krn ship, then fast-forward the main checkout, archive the review series and retire the worktree, all of which deliver normally does.
Acceptance: for a PR whose diff touches only tasks/*.json and whose commits carry no Change-contract, deliver builds the merge message with exactly `Change-contract: none (tracker records only; no executable surface; krn task check runs in the gate)` and completes the same stages as for a code PR; a PR that touches any other path with no commit contract is still refused. Observer: a deliver message test red at the base by assertion for the tracker-only case, green at head, with the refusal case unchanged.
Lead trap: krn-lead says tracker commits carry no Change-contract until this ships.

Do (measure each, keep only what cuts push->Check wall-clock or flakes):
1. Faster runners (Blacksmith 4/8 vCPU as t3code) — needs the Blacksmith GitHub App installed on krn-works: operator action, ask once with a ready link.
2. Cache the toolchain (node/pnpm/mise pnpm install, Go with cache: true) instead of mise install per shard.
3. Rebalance shards (3-4 vs 6-8, slowest shard 129 s) by recorded durations (#244 / t-3trwjr9 planner).
4. Sparse checkout + fetch-depth 2 in Changes.
5. Later: test-task cache with verify-hits.

title: Make the required gate fast for low-risk PRs and stop reporting a slow gate as red
body:
Outcome: a small, low-risk PR reaches a green required `krn/gate` in minutes, not tens of minutes, and deliver never reports a slow gate as a failure.
Operator mandate 2026-11-05 (verbatim): "strukturalnie musisz wszystko ogarnąć ten kod ma być perfekcyjny szefie" — granted after the lead proposed a diff-scoped gate for low-risk changes, which amends ADR 0014 D30 (full Product `krn/gate` required on every HEAD); record the amendment in the ADR in the same PR.
Facts:
- Main `krn/gate` took 12-13 min on the last 6 merges; PR #232 (3-line fix, t-vrbgwbk) ran 40+ min at host load 25 on 16 cores.
- Rootless containerd.service had CPUWeight=20; raised to 400 on 2026-11-05 (~/AGENTS.network.md). Measure gate time after the change before scoping.
- deliver exited 74 "ci: bounded wait timed out" while the gate was still in_progress: the same code as a red gate. A timeout must be a distinct, resumable outcome (or wait to the gate's own deadline).
Steps: (1) profile gate stages from Jenkins (which stage takes the 12 min); (2) fix the deliver timeout exit; (3) propose and implement the tiered gate (risk tier from `krn review --risk-tier`: low = affected tests + rules + preflight, full suite on main after merge) with the D30 amendment.
Proof: an observer for the deliver timeout outcome; a gate-duration measurement before/after on the same PR shape.

Reference (operator, 2026-11-05: pingdotgg/t3code release.yml screenshot + Theo/Astrid posts): wall clock comes from parallelism and skipped work, not fast tests. (a) cheap preflight 31 s and quality checks 49 s gate first, fail fast; (b) server tests sharded into an 8-job matrix, ~2 min each; (c) content-addressed skips: 'Check if the Rust blob is cached' builds only on a new input hash; the cache lives in R2 instead of GitHub cache to avoid evictions; (d) pnpm store cached (Astrid: their pnpm install alone took longer than Theo's build). For KRN: shard the gate suite across parallel containers by measured file duration; cache test results keyed by the hash of each test file's import closure + toolchain, skip unchanged; persist the pnpm store and node_modules by lockfile hash; order stages cheap-first. Measure each step separately (one change at a time).

resolution.note: thread/start turns off hooks, plugins, apps and every MCP server; live first call 19,630 -> 18,954 input tokens, zero hook/MCP frames

title: Worker app-server threads start the operator's MCP servers and run the lead's Codex hooks
body:
Evidence (2026-11-08, #393 first live recording of codex-cli 0.167.0, deleted after review because it carried account data): every worker thread started the 5 MCP servers of the operator's Codex home (figma, asana, builder-vm, node_repl, krn) and ran 4 user hooks from ~/.codex/hooks.json ("KRN: loading the outco…") around each turn. The first model call of a two-line brief took 19,630 uncached input tokens (test/fixtures/codex-app-server/compact.rpc, first thread/tokenUsage/updated). A worker needs neither: the lead's hooks put lead context into a worker turn, and MCP tool schemas widen every call.
Acceptance: worker threads start no MCP server and run no user hook while keeping auth (a thread/start config override, or a worker Codex home holding only auth by reference, never a copied secret). Proof: a live run with mcpServer/startupStatus/updated, hook/started and hook/completed left out of the driver's opt-out list shows none of them, and the PR reports the first-call inputTokens of `KRN_LIVE=1 node scripts/live-worker.mjs --record` before and after.

2026-11-08 research (t-cz92be6): two mechanisms with evidence. (1) Per-thread or launch-level overrides: features.hooks=false, features.plugins=false, features.apps=false and mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false for every name from `codex mcp list --json`, built in one function used by both the spawn and the identity check; on 0.167.0 a launch-level `-c` with an unknown key exits 1, so the override list fails closed (findings CX1 in .krn/runs/lead/t3code-agentic/lanes/t3-codex-driver.md, RP-01 in .krn/runs/lead/external-patterns/lanes/ext-repos.md). (2) A private CODEX_HOME with auth.json and auth.lock symlinked to the operator's files and a minimal config without skills, plugins or MCP servers (RP-04, Every's compound-engineering skill-eval cell). t3code does not isolate: its shadow home isolates auth only and its app-server threads get the operator's MCP servers and hooks (t3-codex-driver.md, Answers). Proof idea: a recorded run, or the mock-provider test of t-m1jmgcv, shows zero hook/started and mcpServer/startupStatus/updated frames and a first-call input token count below the 19,630 in test/fixtures/codex-app-server/compact.rpc.

resolution.note: identifier index after compaction; recall 0.72 vs 0.61 summary on 33 boundaries

title: Re-inject a mechanical identifier index after Claude compaction
body:
Source: finding PA05 of t-cz92be6 (`.krn/runs/lead/external-patterns/lanes/*/findings.json`), ranked first in the memory sector by the t-8hnmfr9 sector plan. It is the only memory step measurable now: it needs no FR-40 power (`evals/fr40/validity.json`: below-power, do not build FR-40).
Problem: after compaction the lead re-discovers paths, SHAs, PR numbers and task ids by reading files again; the paper cited in PA05 measures LLM summaries keeping at most 16.0% of recurring details against 79.1% for a mechanical identifier index.
Deliver: a Claude SessionStart(compact) hook that parses `transcript_path` for paths, SHAs, PR numbers, task ids and error types (at most 40 per type, newest first) and adds a block of at most 1.5 KB beside the handoff Resume block; offline, no model calls. An offline evaluator replays local compaction boundaries.
Acceptance: on at least 15 local compaction boundaries the index recalls at least 0.70 of the identifiers used in the next 3 to 8 tool calls, with the summary-only baseline printed beside it; the block stays at most 1.5 KB; a missing or unreadable transcript degrades to no block with exit 0. Codex parity stays with t-b6v615x.

Delivered: scripts/claude/identifier-index.ts feeds SessionStart(compact) through scripts/claude/context-restart.ts; evals/compact-index/run.ts replays local boundaries. Result on 33 KRN boundaries (main and subagent transcripts, 207 reused identifiers): index recall 0.720, summary-only 0.609, max block 1500 B; half-life 500/1000/2000 gives 0.72/0.72/0.70. Every local project (--all, 366 boundaries): index 0.532, summary 0.451. The block budget, not ranking, bound recall: global greedy fill and brace-tree paths raised 0.66 to 0.72.

Symptom: `npm test -- <those 4 files>` never exits (3 parallel groups + 1 serial file; process tree stays inside nested isolation-gate runners, killed only by timeout). In CI it ran a nested whole-suite for 16 min until the 20-minute job timeout (PR #262 first attempts, shard 6/8, runs 42384155131 and 42384990325).
Repro (observed): planTestShards in scripts/lib/test-shards.mjs seeded shardWeights with the serial files before assigning parallel files (`for (const [position,file] of finalSerialFiles.entries()) shardWeights[position % shardCount % effectiveShards] += weight`), which changes which parallel file lands in which group. With that seeding: `KRN_TEST_OUTPUT=failures timeout 150 npm test -- test/verdict/evaluator-surface.test.ts test/verdict/verdict-owner-hardening.test.ts test/worker/report-outcome.test.ts test/trace/index.test.ts` -> exit 124 every time (4 of 4). Without the seeding, plain LPT order -> exit 0 in ~49 s; origin/main -> 48 s. Each file alone passes (1-50 s); pairs and triples with trace/index also pass. The exact group-to-file assignment was not printed, so the offending ordering is not pinned down; the seeding patch was dropped, so reproduce by re-applying it or by permuting the group order in planTestShards.
Suspect: a hidden shared resource between concurrent groups (worker/report-outcome spawns `krn worker start`; verdict tests use bwrap; trace/index asserts lock timings), only exposed by a particular group index assignment.
Done when: the 4 files pass in every group order (add a test that runs them under permuted group assignment) or the shared resource is isolated per worker.

resolution.note: Test shards no longer download mise or pnpm from GitHub releases

title: Keep CI test shards working when GitHub release downloads return 5xx
body:
Outcome: an outage of github.com release downloads no longer fails the Test shards: the mise binary and the pinned package manager come from a cache or a fallback route, verified by checksum.
Evidence: main run 42468167813 (head 0486d86, after #395): attempt 1 failed 7 of 10 Test shards (1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10) in `Set up mise`, attempt 2 failed 4 of them (4, 7, 8, 10); the Test 8/10 log shows `curl -fsSL https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/download/v2026.10.17/mise-v2026.10.17-linux-x64.tar.zst` failing with exit code 22 under the action's own retry loop (`Retrying in 2 seconds (1/5)`), so in-action retries exist and do not bridge a multi-minute outage; the release route answered 302 again when probed later and https://mise.jdx.dev/v2026.10.17/mise-v2026.10.17-linux-x64.tar.zst answers 200. .github/workflows/ci.yml:121-126 sets `cache: false`; ci.yml:128-133 installs the pinned package manager with `mise install`; project-ci.yml:93,115,144 use the same action. flake-census.md has no entry for this class; t-2f4cqda and t-nwdj5hx measured toolchain caching for speed only.
Source: lead observation while reading main CI during t-cz92be6; flake census .krn/runs/lead/weakness-hunt/flake-census.md has no entry for this class.
Acceptance: the mise download lives in one script (scripts/ci/install-mise.mjs) called by ci.yml (project-ci.yml follows only if still used); a node:test runs it against a local HTTP server: when the primary URL answers 504 and the fallback URL (mise.jdx.dev route or a cache hit) serves the real artifact, the script installs from the fallback after at most one failed primary attempt and exits 0; when the artifact's SHA-256 differs from the pinned checksum it exits non-zero and installs nothing; on the PR run, the `Set up mise` step p50 (node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs) stays within 2 s of its value on main.

Delivered differently than the acceptance proposed: the shards used mise only for `mise where pnpm` (scripts/test-suite.mjs parentPnpmStoreDirectory), and `mise install pnpm` also downloads from github.com releases, so a mise fallback alone would still fail. The test job now drops both mise steps and setup-ci exports pnpm_config_store_dir from the Corepack pnpm (npm registry), so the shards download nothing from GitHub releases and the Set up mise step time goes to zero; test/workflow.test.ts asserts the test job names no mise. project-ci.yml (adopter workflow) keeps mise-action because adopters pin their tools there.

title: Build FR-40 arm material: brain records, packets and static standards

What: the minimal ADR 0002 record shape (id, type, text, recorded_at, valid_from, valid_to, source) as reviewed JSON files, built from sources dated before the task base (ADRs, docs/program, decisions log, closed task bodies); a deterministic packet builder (D32: a Product module outside core under its own command, shadow packets under `.krn/`, never injected outside FR-40 arms) that selects records by task text with recorded_at ≤ base date and a fixed token budget; arm S material: the same token budget of static AGENTS.md/workflow standards, identical for every task.

title: Clear stale tool results from long lead contexts
body:
Outcome: KRN lead sessions drop stale bulky tool results from context through a mechanism Claude Code supports, or the task records with evidence that none exists and what the nearest lever is.
Why: Anthropic context management (https://claude.com/blog/context-management): context editing cut tokens 84% on a 100-turn eval and raised task success 29%. KRN lead cache reads are 41% of lead $ at median 85k context per turn (lead-cost scan 2026-11-09).
Proof: the Claude Code documentation or binary shows the setting or hook (PostToolUse output replacement, compaction settings, clear_tool_uses); if one exists, it is enabled in .claude/settings.json with a test, and a before/after per-turn context median is recorded.
Scope: .claude/settings.json, scripts/claude, docs/program, test.

## Finding (claude 2.1.319, binary /home/krn/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.319/claude)
No user-enableable lever drops stale tool results from the lead context.
- Server-side clearing exists but is remote-flagged: `grep -a clear_tool_uses` hits `clear_tool_uses_20250919` edits planned only after idle (`tengu_tool_result_clearing_after_idle_planned`); mode comes from `Rdr()` = flag `tengu_jiggly_blossom`, values on|shadow|off, default off. No settings.json key or env var sets it (`grep -a -o CLAUDE_CODE_[A-Z_]*TOOL_RESULT` finds only CLAUDE_CODE_TRANSCRIPT_SLIM_TOOL_RESULTS, a transcript-file option).
- PostToolUse `updatedToolOutput` ("Replaces the tool output before it is sent to the model", binary schema; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) rewrites only the result of the call that just ran, not earlier results, so it cannot clear stale ones.
- Compaction levers are whole-context only: autoCompactWindow (already 400000), CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, CLAUDE_CODE_SLEEP_COMPACT*, CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS.
## Nearest lever (already in place)
Prevent bulk instead of clearing it: PreToolUse scripts/claude/lead-file-read.ts refuses large cat/sed/grep/Read dumps for the lead; BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=12000 caps Bash output. A PostToolUse truncation would duplicate these and lose data the model needs on the turn it arrives.
## Measure if the flag ever turns on
Median per-turn context from the transcript usage (input+cache_read+cache_creation) via scripts/claude/context-report.ts, before vs after; applied_edits of type clear_tool_uses_20250919 appear in message.context_management.

Outcome: test/claude/successor-launch.test.ts, successor-retire.test.ts and successor-handed-off.test.ts serve their verbatim Herdr captures from a /bin/sh stub that runs only shell builtins, like the stub in test/claude/successor-probe.test.ts, so a launcher change runs its tests in seconds locally and in CI.
Evidence: a node-script stub costs 57 ms per call against 4 ms for a builtin-only sh stub (20-call bench on the lead host, 2026-11-08). The three files take 7978, 11370 and 3329 ms locally (22.7 s; CI medians 3.6, 8.4 and 2.7 s in scripts/lib/shard-weights.mjs), while successor-probe.test.ts runs the real launcher over 11 paths with about 13 sh stub calls each in 891 ms. It starts after t-wm22s14 so the shard window measures one plan.
Proof: every assertion and capture stays; the three files sum below 9 s of local duration_ms on the lead host (baseline 22.7 s), and their refreshed CI weights drop.

The shard window it waited on closed 5 of 5 since e9ebc8f (FAIL, see t-wm22s14), so this stub no longer perturbs a window; it now lands before the next shard refresh so the refresh folds its durations (successor-retire ran at a 12.4 s CI median in that window, over the 11 s file bound).

title: Treat stale agent instructions as blocking review findings
body:
Operator (2026-11-06, on PR #247 review "NON_BLOCKING .agents/skills/krn-lead/SKILL.md:35 Instrukcja nadal wskazuje stare wymagane sprawdzenie"): "jak to non-blocking, to mega ważne jest szefunciu".
Defect class: an agent instruction (AGENTS.md, skills, docs/program, briefs) that names a mechanism the same PR retires or replaces. Agents follow instructions literally, so a stale instruction is a correctness defect, not style. On #247 the panel rated it NON_BLOCKING and the lead nearly delivered it.
Do:
1. Review panel: findings about instructions contradicting the PR's own change are BLOCKING (judge prompt + hardening checklist class).
2. Deterministic check: when spec/ci-admission.json (or another selector) changes, agent instructions must not name the old selector except in history/ADR text — preflight observer.
3. Lead rule: the lead never ships a NON_BLOCKING finding on agent instructions without fixing it or recording why.
Proof: replay PR #247 record .krn/runs/review-series/4a397cd3…/records/1.json — the finding must come out BLOCKING; the observer fails on archive/ci-actions-cb072e9 and passes on the fixed head.

title: Audit: make KRN delivery cheaper than plain git+gh
body:
Operator 2026-11-06 ~23:00Z: "nie uważasz że normalnie bez krn lepiej się pracuje niż z krn? musisz zrobić audyt i tak ogarnąć system żeby realnie lepiej się pracowało z krn niż normalnie" and "Naprawiaj wszystko, musisz penetrować to do tego stopnia żeby Ci się zajebiście dobrze pracowało".
Goal: KRN delivery must be measurably cheaper than plain git+gh+tests. Metric: wall-clock and lead tokens from "change ready" to "merged + main green" for a one-file fix; plain baseline ~15 min.
Evidence from the 2026-11-06 session (t-9czzfve, a ~20-line ship fix) that took ~3 h of lead time:
1. Orphaned Jenkins krn/gate blocked Product ship (fixed in GLOBAL #477, sealed #478 = b41faae, NOT installed).
2. Host install blocked: ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md are operator-owned files, six ~/.agents/skills KRN links were removed; `krn install apply` exits 73 (foreign collision). Workaround used: PATH shim `krn` -> GLOBAL checkout at b41faae for `krn deliver`. Decide: retire managed AGENTS.md/skills from the GLOBAL manifest or port ship into Product so legacy forwarding is not on the delivery path.
3. GLOBAL CI still on Jenkins (required gate (fast)/(deep), app 5548482): no webhook delivery (manual branch-indexing scans via tunnel), gate (fast) flaky "session pids limit probe" on the first build. Blocks Jenkins/PVE decommission t-sdcdxb2.
4. GLOBAL judges krn/judge-standards/spec must be posted by hand from the review record; Product deliver refuses a GLOBAL PR (exit 71 Node pin).
5. Review red-first sandbox leaks task slots (t-g1nr12w) -> false head=assertion.
6. GLOBAL quality:audit fails on a dynamically imported export ("dead export").
7. Main CI flake family t-r69gyb7 hit again (codex-usage-completeness "Codex startup cancelled before registration"), needed gh run rerun.
8. Two repos, two trackers of truth, two delivery CLIs; the lead reads huge JSON blobs (review output, Jenkins HTML) by default.
Do: an audit of every step a lead takes for a one-file fix (enumerate mechanically; time each), compare to plain git/gh, then delete or automate every step that does not catch real defects. Candidates: one CLI for both repos, ship inside Product, Actions for GLOBAL, review prints a one-line verdict, deliver posts judge statuses for any repo, flake quarantine.

Operator 2026-11-07 (verbatim): "Potem najważniejsze jest porównanie t3 headless i badanie AB ale najpierw ogarnij te wszystkie najważniejsze rzeczy.." and "musimy udowodnic ze lepszy niz przy normalnej pracy". Next after the current batch: headless A/B on the same task set, arms KRN lead vs plain git+gh vs T3 headless (t3 thread start --wait), metrics wall time, USD/tokens, defects reaching main, red Check rounds; reuse .krn/runs/lead/t3-ab/ harness.

title: Report a successor that waits on a startup dialog
body:
Outcome: the launcher's success line shows the successor's first settled Herdr status, and a successor waiting on a startup dialog (`blocked`) is reported to the operator with its pane instead of passing as a clean handoff.
Evidence: the t-p4akh87 live probe (Herdr 0.9.1, untrusted scratch cwd) printed `successor: herdr tab w1D:tAR pane w1D:pAX agent claude unknown` within 3 s while the pane sat on Claude's folder-trust dialog; `herdr agent get` reported `blocked` seconds later. A project MCP approval or a login prompt would stall a real handoff the same way. The official `agent start` fails with agent_not_ready on such a dialog while the agent is live, so failing the launch risks a duplicate successor (t-tdkpgag): report, do not fail.
Proof: a test with a verbatim blocked `agent get` capture (redacted per test/fixtures/README.md) where the new pane goes from unknown to blocked prints `agent claude blocked` and exits 0; the krn-handoff skill tells the predecessor to name that pane in its report.

Live probe: run the launcher from a scratch Herdr tab whose pane hosts only a shell (herdr tab create --cwd <scratch> --no-focus; herdr pane run <pane> 'KRN_SUCCESSOR_AGENT=claude node <repo>/scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts ...'), never from the lead's pane: a lead caller gets its tab renamed and the probe successor's --retire closes the lead pane once idle. A shell caller has no agent, so the launcher skips the rename, the ledger and the predecessor env; close both tabs afterwards. An untrusted scratch cwd holds the probe on the folder-trust dialog, so it spends no tokens.

body:

title: Gate controller retries GitHub 5xx and always completes the krn/gate check
body:
Outcome: a transient GitHub API error at the end of a Product gate build never leaves `krn/gate` in_progress forever; the controller retries 5xx with bounded backoff, and a terminal failure still completes the check (failure, summary `failed at stage <stage>: <cause>`) so deliver can rerun at once.
Evidence (PR #232, head de9f3dc, 2026-11-05): Jenkins ci/product/PR-232 #1 ran all stages in 787 s (17:06-17:19Z), then `ci.Controller.requireCurrentHead` (Controller.groovy:296 via ownedCi.groovy:229) got `HttpException: Service Unavailable` from `GHRepository.getPullRequest`; publishChecks logged "Failure check publication is unverified" and the check stayed in_progress 70+ min; deliver exited 74 "ci: bounded wait timed out". Diagnosis: .krn/runs/lead/t-vrbgwbk/gate-stuck.md.
This is ci-platform production code: deploying the fix needs the deployment owner's grant (batch with t-6997d21, t-33mv33n). Related: t-47enn80 (deliver timeout outcome).
Proof: a controller test where getPullRequest throws 503 twice then succeeds (passes) and always throws (check completed as failure with the stage named).

Also: `krn ci rerun` exits 75 'check run is still in_progress' when the Jenkins build already finished but the check was never completed; the lead had to POST the native job /build (201, new check 127442328242). rerun must read the Jenkins build state, not only the GitHub check status.

Lead trap: when `krn/gate` stays in_progress after the Jenkins build finished, `krn ci rerun` exits 75; POST the native `/job/ci/job/product/job/PR-<n>/build` through the lead tunnel instead (never re-push).

title: Universal repository standards reach every project on the host without imposing KRN process

Why: operator 2026-11-14 (verbatim): "wyłącz również w koncu skillsy globalne zeby nie affectować contextu, najlepsze standardy realizowane w tym repo powinny być również globalne". The repository's standards live in .agents/conventions.json (r-* records), .agents/standards.json (one s-* standard) and the project skills architecture and typescript; none reaches a project that has not run krn adopt. The global contract (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) forbids imposing a workflow or tracker on a project that has not adopted one, so only stack-agnostic engineering standards may go global, never KRN process (tracker, lanes, ship).

title: Generate FR-40 convention tasks with deterministic scorers
body:
FR-40 slice 1 of 4 (parent t-y46gy0w; operator GO 2026-11-08, .krn/runs/lead/decisions.md). Convention tasks and their deterministic scorers.
What: a generator under evals/fr40/ that emits synthetic convention tasks against a fixed KRN base, each with a prompt and one scorer that reads only the scratch repository after the session (git log, diff, filesystem) and prints pass/fail. Conventions with a mechanical check: task id at the end of the commit title; `Ticket:` vs `Refs:` trailer by whether the task closes; agent state only under `.krn/` (KRN-08); worker never edits `tasks/*.json` (KRN-11); core imports stay in core (`scripts/boundaries.ts`, KRN-05); unknown CLI command exits 64 (KRN-06); names by role, not task id or date; Biome clean. Prefer conventions recorded outside `AGENTS.md` (docs/program/repository-workflow.md, ADRs, lead decisions) so the packet arm can matter while AGENTS.md is on in every arm.
Independence: units sharing a template are one cluster. Record template ids; `evals/fr40/power.ts` must accept the cluster count and the slice reports whether the template set reaches 0.8 power at discordance 0.05–0.15 (74–132 units in evals/fr40/validity.json). If it cannot, stop and report to the operator before slice 2.
Constraints: no file under evals/fr40 may contain the forbidden SHA prefixes (test/evals/fr40-validity.test.ts). Scorers are tested against hand-made passing and failing scratch repos (KRN-12, KRN-14).
Acceptance: `node evals/fr40/<generator>` emits ≥74 tasks with template ids; each template has a scorer test with one pass and one fail case; the power report for the template clustering is recorded in evals/fr40/.

title: Cut agent token cost: mid-step relay, 44k baseline, Opus leaks
body:
Outcome: agent sessions on this host stop paying for oversized context: no session runs past the relay threshold, Opus runs only where chosen, and a fresh session starts well below ~44k tokens.
Evidence (operator usage audit 2026-11-09, API-price estimates, not per account): 794 sessions, ~104k requests, active 150 of 168 h/week, ~9 concurrent sessions; Opus ~89% of cost; requests above 200k context ~39% of cost; 44 sessions passed 300k (~20%), 8 reached 964k (~11%) because context-relay measures only after a finished step, so one long step crosses the threshold without a handoff; ekologus-wp-local agents frontend-artist and slice-reviewer pin model: opus (~9% of cost); some general-purpose subagents ran on Opus despite CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=sonnet (cause unknown); cswap auto does not rotate accounts, so account 3 hit 100%; a fresh session starts at ~44k tokens resent on every request.
Acceptance: (1) the context check fires during a step, not only after it (a PreToolUse/PostToolUse measurement that forces handoff at the threshold), proven by a transcript replay that crosses it mid-step; (2) the 44k baseline is broken down by source (system prompt, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, memory index, skills listing, MCP tools) and the KRN-owned share cut; (3) the subagent-model override cause is found from transcripts with a reproduction; (4) out-of-repo items (ekologus agents pinned to opus, cswap auto rotation, global skills) are listed with a decision-ready proposal for the operator, since they sit outside KRN scope and global config.
Note: operator asked to take this on after t-wm22s14 (2026-11-09).

Acceptance 1 evidence (#456, 724ded0): scripts/claude/context-replay.ts replays a transcript through the real gauge hook; fixture test proves the advisory lands mid-step (243k, step ended 273k). KRN transcript peaks: 966k before the PostToolUse gauge (2026-10-29), at most 343k since; other projects without the gauge still reach 964-967k. Host replay of 77 transcripts over 300k: .krn/runs/token-audit/mid-step-replay.jsonl (running detached, done when .krn/runs/token-audit/replay.done exists). First 10: every first advisory fired mid-step at 240-242k, but steps ran on to 260-368k, so an advisory alone does not stop a long step; next slice: a forcing check (repeat or PreToolUse refusal above a ceiling) plus a host-wide gauge install proposal for the operator (global hooks need hook trust).

Acceptance 1 forcing check: context-gauge repeats the second advisory every 10k of growth and, past 90% of autoCompactWindow, a PreToolUse hook refuses Agent/Task/Workflow/WebFetch/WebSearch/NotebookEdit and Write/Edit outside .krn/ and ~/.claude/projects (Bash, Read, Skill stay open for krn-handoff). Proof: test/claude/context-replay.test.ts refuses an Agent call at 243k inside the step that reached 273k; host replay of the 5 transcripts over 360k: .krn/runs/token-audit/ceiling-replay.jsonl.

Ceiling replay (ecd3791, .krn/runs/token-audit/ceiling-replay.jsonl, 5 transcripts over 360k): the ceiling refused 1-42 calls, but first refusals landed at 360-476k because sessions grow past the ceiling through Bash and Read, which stay open for the handoff. Next: past the ceiling, refuse Bash commands outside a handoff allowlist (krn state, krn task, git, handoff-requests, operator-inbox, successor-launch) and cap Read output, proven by the same replay.

Handoff-only ceiling: past 90% the gauge admits only Skill, ToolSearch, Bash built from handoff commands (cd, echo, krn, git, node scripts/claude/{handoff-requests,operator-inbox,successor-launch}.ts, no substitutions), reads and writes under .krn/ or memory, and Read with limit <= 200; every other tool is refused. Replay (.krn/runs/token-audit/ceiling-bash-replay.jsonl, 6 transcripts over 360k at a 400k window, ceiling 360k; PreToolUse now evaluated in process): first refusal at 360-365k in all six (was 360-477k), refusals 10-467, admitted handoff calls 0-13. Acceptance 2 (baseline by source): npm run context:report now prints baseline tokens per prompt source and the largest tool schemas. Fresh interactive KRN session 2026-11-09 (42.5k measured): harness tool schemas 30.5k (Artifact 14.6k, SendFeedback 2.3k, Workflow 2.2k, ScheduleWakeup 2.0k, Agent 2.0k, AskUserQuestion 1.8k), skill listing 4.3k, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md+memory instructions 2.1k, system prompt 2.1k, agent listing 1.3k, SessionStart hook 0.4k. title: Make Actions CI faster than t3code (all Theo tricks allowed)
body:
Operator grant (2026-11-06, verbatim): "wszystkie triki od theo są dozwolone szefie, to musi być superior tool".
Baseline: KRN Actions CI median PR 451 s / main push 475 s (gh run list), #247 run 42228642474 ~174 s start->Check; t3code PR median 226 s. Recon: .krn/runs/lead/ci-actions/t3code-recon.md.
Do (measure each, keep only what cuts push->Check wall-clock or flakes):
1. Faster runners (Blacksmith 4/8 vCPU as t3code) — needs the Blacksmith GitHub App installed on krn-works: operator action, ask once with a ready link.
2. Cache the toolchain (node/pnpm/mise pnpm install, Go with cache: true) instead of mise install per shard.
3. Wider change detection: docs-only (**/*.md outside spec) skips Test; keep Check fail-closed (skip ok only when changes says false).
4. Isolation (bubblewrap/sysctl/apt) and Go only on shards/paths that need them; then rebalance shards (3-4 vs 6-8, slowest shard 129 s) by recorded durations (#244 / t-3trwjr9 planner).
5. Sparse checkout + fetch-depth 2 in Changes; concurrency cancel-in-progress already present.
6. Later: test-task cache with verify-hits.
Proof: median push->Check over >=10 PR runs before/after in .krn/runs/lead/ci-actions/speed.md; target <= t3code median.
Also move rules render + krn task check to local preflight only if CI keeps an equivalent cheap Lint step (rules are gate inputs; decide by measurement).

Operator decision (2026-11-06, verbatim): "Zdecydowanie wdrażamy: ... t3code w CI tylko weryfikuje. Release, preview i testy Windows siedzą w osobnych workflow, poza bramką ... render reguł, task check oraz testy izolacji i Go [przenieść do lokalnego preflight albo uruchamiać tylko na właściwych ścieżkach] - zrób to asap." Settled: the required Check verifies only; anything not verification lives in separate workflows outside the gate; rules render + task check move to local preflight; isolation (bubblewrap/systemd) and Go tests run only when their paths change. Proof still by measurement (push->Check median before/after). In progress: branch ci/slim-gate, worktree .krn/worktrees/ci-slim (uncommitted: scripts/ci-changes.mjs, test/ci/ci-changes.test.ts, ci.yml isolation output + KRN_TEST_EXCLUDE_ISOLATION, Lint drops rules/task check). Measured on run of 047aeb3: Go+bubblewrap+sysctl setup ~14-16 s per shard, rules+task check ~1 s.

title: Shard, cache and tier the required gate so low-risk PRs go green in minutes
body:
Outcome: a small, low-risk PR reaches a green required `krn/gate` in minutes, not tens of minutes. Continues t-47enn80 (slice 1 shipped the deliver ci-wait exit 75 and the gate profile).
Operator mandate 2026-11-05 (verbatim): "strukturalnie musisz wszystko ogarnąć ten kod ma być perfekcyjny szefie" — granted after the lead proposed a diff-scoped gate for low-risk changes, which amends ADR 0014 D30 (full Product `krn/gate` required on every HEAD); record the amendment in the ADR in the same PR as the tiered gate.
Profile (.krn/runs/lead/t-47enn80/gate-profile.md, PR-232 #2): the VM `npm run gate` unit (check, lint, test, task check, rules, run serially) ran 11 min 30 s of a ~13 min build; infra overhead ~1 min; PR builds took 7.5-8 min before host load. The gate stdout artifact is cut at 4096 bytes, so per-file test durations are not yet measured.
Slices, one measured change each: (1) export per-file test durations from the gate (evidence artifact) and measure; (2) shard the gate suite across parallel containers by measured duration, cheap stages first, fail fast; (3) content-hash test-result cache keyed by each test file's import closure + toolchain, skip unchanged; (4) persist the pnpm store and node_modules by lockfile hash; (5) tiered gate from `krn review --risk-tier` (low = affected tests + rules + preflight, full suite on main after merge) with the D30 amendment.
Reference (operator, 2026-11-05: pingdotgg/t3code release.yml): wall clock comes from parallelism and skipped work, not fast tests: cheap preflight first, 8-job sharded tests, content-addressed skips with an eviction-free cache, cached pnpm store.
Proof: a gate-duration measurement before/after on the same PR shape for each slice.

title: Intent to task, measured
body:
Outcome: for one week of operator rows in the inbox, the share that became a task, the share whose task closed done, and the time from the prompt to the merge, joined by hand from the "Operator requests" lines of the handoffs.
Why: the brief's first step has no record: nothing joins a prompt to a task. The tracker alone shows 200 of 533 tasks closed other than done, 187 in one triage on 11-07 and 3 of the 164 created since **[V]**; two of the three are intent losses (`t-jzdybq2`, `t-ps3ap2e`), which is a cleared backlog and a first sample, and says nothing about prompts that never became a task.
Proof: a table; if every operator row of the week has a task and at most one in ten is still open after a day, the slice closes with that answer and nothing is built. Otherwise the task records which field (an origin on the task, or a task id on the inbox row) would have made the join mechanical.
Scope: a script under `scripts/claude/`, read-only.
Order: B1, B2, B3; then the two measurements B6 and B7; B4 when the operator adds the line; B5 last.
Order: after B2.
Program: .krn/runs/krn-architecture-program/05-program.md section 4, slice B7.

Measured 2026-11-10 with `node scripts/claude/intent-to-task.ts --from 2026-11-03 --to 2026-11-10 --rows`. The inbox holds rows only from 2026-11-07T14:50Z (315 rows, 3.8 days of the week). 22 are harness wrappers and 183 launcher prompts (98 successor-launch, relay.sh templates and disposition refs naming a launch), leaving 110 operator rows. Of those 25 (23%) joined to a task, 23 of them (92%) closed done, 0 of 25 still open after a day, median prompt to closing merge 0.1 h over 22 rows (max 3.1 h). The other 85: 18 memory, 22 chat answers, 45 with no disposition at all (41%), some real directives. Verdict: not every operator row has a task, so nothing closes by default. The missing field is a task id (or an explicit none) on the inbox row at the moment of disposition: today the join is a free-text ref parsed for t-ids and 45 rows were never disposed, so intent loss is invisible. Caveat: the 0.1 h median is of prompts that already steered work in flight; the join cannot see prompts that started nothing.

title: review depth follows a risk tier of the diff
body:
Outcome: review depth follows risk, not a fixed panel. A deterministic classifier on the diff picks a tier: low (docs, tests, tracker, small non-sensitive code) = deterministic checks + one judge; medium = current panel; high (CI workflows, review/ship/deliver code, ADRs, spec/worker-scope.json) = panel + operator notice. The panel adds voting/dedup of findings, drops style findings and re-reviews only the diff after round one.
Evidence: .krn/runs/lead/market-research/report.md ("How the Claude Code team does code review", 2026-10-15: first-round pass 65%→78%, mean rounds 2.08→1.32); KRN review is the largest wait per slice.
Proof: classifier observer over fixture diffs per tier; panel observer asserting a duplicated finding is reported once and a style finding is dropped.
Decisions: a low tier without the full panel amends ADR 0014 D30 ("Standards and Spec required"); the lead decides it under the Full autonomy grant and records the amendment in the same PR.

Why: on 2026-11-14 at least four lane rebases (lane-drain #781, doctor-host #795, adopt-refresh #797, deploy-safe) hit a conflict in the generated docs/generated/capability-index.md; ship exits 76 and the lane regenerates by hand.

Proof: ship test with a real temp repository where two branches change src headers (conflicting index only) rebases cleanly; npm run fast PASS.

resolution.note: limit_hit counts only claude-reported errors; regression test: a successful arm quoting a limit is not delayed or retried

title: A D23 arm whose output mentions a usage limit is not treated as limit-hit
body:
Why: in the n100 run (2026-11-12) arm 622.P succeeded, but its result text quoted its own task ("hit your 5-hour limit"); replay.sh limit_hit greps the whole claude.json and stderr, so the arm slept the 5 h cap and would be retried and rerun by the driver.
Outcome: an arm counts as limit-hit only when claude reports an error (claude.json is_error true, or no parseable json) and the error text names a usage limit; a successful arm whose output mentions limits is never retried.
Proof: a replay test with a fake claude that succeeds with a result mentioning "hit your 5-hour limit" asserts no wait, no retry and no limit_retry line.
Scope: evals/d23/, test/evals/.

Evidence: PR #206 second round (.krn/runs/lead/review-override/slice-review2b.log): push succeeded, review exited 64 immediately; a rerun minutes later passed admission. Lead trap: when slice review exits 64 'authoritative PR number/base/head does not match' right after a push, check `gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid` equals the local HEAD, then rerun the same slice command; a deliver exit 76 'check runs unavailable' with krn/gate already success is resumed by rerunning deliver.

title: slice run keeps the review series count across a same-ref rebase
body:
Outcome: `krn slice run` resets its review attempt count only when the review series actually starts over; after a rebase onto a new main SHA with the same baseRef it keeps the series count and stops with the budget-exception instruction before calling review.
Evidence: PR #212 (t-sa7ag03): slice run verify reset reviewAttempts to 0 on a new base (src/slice/run.ts "a new base starts a new series"), but the series is keyed by PR and baseRef `main`, so the next review exited 64 "two attempts exhausted"; attempt 3 then ran by hand with --budget-exception, and slice run has no --budget-exception passthrough.
Proof: slice observer: rebase onto a moved main after two FAIL attempts → no review call, exit 64 naming the exception path; with `--budget-exception <file>` the review argv carries it.

title: Rebalance shards from 10-shard CI durations
body:
Outcome: the 10-shard plan stops overloading one shard, so the slowest Test step moves toward the shard mean.
Evidence: main runs since 2194438 (42429805266, 42430428146, 42430864780, 42431526060): shard 3 ran 14/18/18/18 s while shards 1 and 5 ran 10-13 s; node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since 2194438 flags 23 files whose median CI duration exceeds their weight by more than 30% (worst test/worker/hardening-baseline.test.ts 13.2 s vs weight 6.8); both models correlate weakly (summed r=0.35, heaviest-lane r=-0.17).
Acceptance: node scripts/shard-weights-refresh.mjs --runs 5 --write over 10-shard main runs only; then 5 main runs since that commit print a slowest Test step p50 below 18 s and fewer drifted files (node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since <refresh sha>).

Note: Pearson r cannot judge a balanced plan (predicted walls 43.4-43.5 summed and 10.9-11.7 lane s barely vary, so r was 0.35 and -0.20 over 5 runs); judge per-shard medians across runs (shard 3 at 18 s in 3 of 5) and the slowest-step p50, or replace the r verdict in scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs with a shard-rank consistency check.

Refresh e9ebc8f (window start): weights from 10-shard main runs 42437333036 42437063331 42436168431 42436014411 42435706998; test/worker/state-trust.test.ts (12.2 s) and test/worker/recovery.test.ts (11.7 s) split under the 11 s file bound with apportioned weights. Baseline over those runs at 1dd36d6 (node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --runs 5): slowest Test step p50 17 s, 17 drifted files, shard p50 11-16 s (shard 3 highest). On their per-file medians the old plan summed 23.5-55.5 s per shard (lane wall 9.6-14.6 s), the refreshed plan 42.4-42.5 s (lane wall 10.7-11.8 s). Close when node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e9ebc8f prints runs: 5 of 5 with a slowest Test step p50 below 18 s and fewer than 17 drifted files.

Window run 1: main 42438874107 (051c00a) Test steps 8-19 s, slowest 19 s (shard 7); PR run 42438789064 also peaked at 19 s (shard 6). In both runs evals/workspace.test.ts ran 10.6-12.6 s against weight 5.1 beside evals/workspace-mask.test.ts in shard 6, and main shard 7 carried worker/hardening-redaction.test.ts at 11.7 s against 4.3. If the window's drift section keeps flagging same-family files, test family anti-affinity in planTestShards or refresh once more before closing; per-shard p50 comes with t-5fs38a3.

Window verdict, 5 of 5 since e9ebc8f (main 42438874107 42439302711 42440860512 42441356963 42442106709): FAIL. Slowest Test step p50 19 s (target below 18 s, baseline 17 s), 32 drifted files (baseline 17); shard p50: 1/10=14 2/10=14 3/10=14 4/10=19 5/10=9 6/10=16 7/10=16 8/10=12 9/10=13 10/10=18 s; highest 4/10 +4.5 s over the mean 14.5 s. The shard rank follows each shard's longest file, not its summed weight: 4/10 holds test/worker/acceptance-checks-reruns.test.ts at a 15.5 s CI median (weight 10.1) and 10/10 holds test/worker/acceptance-checks-observers.test.ts at 14.2 s (weight 8.8); the 11 s file bound passed on weights that lag CI by up to 53%, so the report now prints a 'files over the 11 s bound' line from CI medians and gates the slowest p50 at 18 s. Next, after t-dddwdtg lands: split every file that line lists, refresh from 10-shard main runs that include the splits, and open a new window; close when node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since <refresh sha> prints runs: 5 of 5, 'target < 18 s: PASS', 'files over the 11 s bound: none' and fewer than 17 drifted files.

Refresh e79cb01 (window start): weights from 10-shard main runs 42445125280 42444826902 42443183605 42443064364 42442826299; the three files on the e9ebc8f report's 'files over the 11 s bound' line split by theme with apportioned weights: acceptance-checks-observers 7.9 + acceptance-checks-containment 6.5 (parent 14.4 s), acceptance-checks-reruns 6.4 + acceptance-checks-validation 6.3 (parent 12.7 s), hardening-redaction 7.2 + hardening-allow 4.6 (parent 11.8 s). Baseline: node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e9ebc8f at d2a2baf printed slowest Test step p50 18 s (FAIL), shard 4/10 highest at 18 s, 26 drifted files. On those CI medians the main plan's lane walls span 7.8-17.6 s, the refreshed plan's 11.1-12.0 s. Close when node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e79cb01 prints runs: 5 of 5, 'target < 18 s: PASS', 'files over the 11 s bound: none' and fewer than 17 drifted files.

Window run 1: main 42446268339 (af9afa4) cleared the three split files from the bound line (acceptance-checks-validation 8.6 s vs weight 6.3 is the family's only drift), yet the slowest Test step rose to 20 s (shard 7; shard 4 at 18 s). Shard 7 co-located input-bounds-baseline 17.4 s (weight 8.7), input-bounds-persisted 12.0 s (9.3), acceptance-checks-validation 8.6 s and acceptance-checks-reruns 7.1 s; shard 2 ran input-bounds-ignored at 3.7 s against weight 10.1. At equal planned weight sums (43.9-44.0) shards ran 0.65x-1.39x their weights, so a file's CI time follows the load co-located with it. If the window fails with same-family files sharing the slow shards, the next lever is family anti-affinity in planTestShards, not another split. A PASS also needs every Test step timed (t-67jrrez).

At 183dcf3, node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e79cb01 printed runs 3 of 5 and FAIL at a 20 s p50, with Test (7/10) the slowest step in all three runs (20, 20 and 21 s) and input-bounds-baseline (17.4 s) and input-bounds-persisted (12 s) over the 11 s bound. Three of five samples at 20 s or more put the 5-run median at 20 s or more, so the e79cb01 window is decided FAIL; family anti-affinity in planTestShards is next without waiting for 5 of 5.

Family spread 7866a48 (window start: 80f75bf plus the test-suite-speed split): planTestShards puts each file in a bin holding the fewest files of its family (testFileFamily: one directory, same first word), the lightest of those. Evidence: input-bounds-baseline and input-bounds-persisted ran 17.4 and 12.2 s side by side in Test (7/10) of the e79cb01 window against 8.7 and 9.3 s on separate runners in the e9ebc8f window; evals/workspace ran 10.6-12.6 s beside evals/workspace-mask against 5.1 s apart. test-suite-speed (10.8-12.0 s beside nontechnical-blocker in 3/10, 6.5-9.0 s in 5/10 before) splits into test-suite-speed 3.9 + test-suite-failures 3.3 (parent 7.2 s by local medians 5.17/4.40 s); other weights stay, as the input-bounds medians come from runs where those files ran apart. On the weights the 10-runner plan holds no same-family pair (was 13) at summed walls 11.0-11.0 s and heaviest lanes 7.7-11.5 s (was 7.7-11.4). Baseline: node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since e79cb01 at 49dacad printed runs 4 of 5, slowest Test step p50 20 s (FAIL), shard 7/10 at 20 s, files over the 11 s bound input-bounds-baseline 17.4 s, input-bounds-persisted 12.2 s, test-suite-speed 11.3 s, 24 drifted files. Close when node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since 7866a48 prints runs: 5 of 5, 'target < 18 s: PASS', 'files over the 11 s bound: none' and fewer than 17 drifted files; if the p50 sits within 1 s of 18 s, land t-953mdqx first.

Window run 1: main 42449443692 (9235996) printed slowest Test step 16 s (target < 18 s: PASS), shard p50 9-16 s with mean 12.1 s (e79cb01 window 14.2 s), 13 drifted files (was 24) and one file over the 11 s bound, worker/session.test.ts at 11.7 s against weight 9.5; the highest shard was 1/10 at 16 s, the runner that carries the serial codex-stale-scope. No input-bounds, test-suite or workspace file drifted. PR run 42449373341 peaked at 17 s (shards 5 and 6). Watch worker/session over the next runs before acting on one sample.

Window run 3: main 42450770597 (b663e29, #387) makes 3 of 5. On log-precision step times (t-953mdqx) node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since 7866a48 prints 'slowest Test step p50: 15.5 s, target < 18 s: PASS, decided', shard p50 9.6-15.3 s (highest 2/10 +2.8 s over the mean 12.5 s), no file over the 11 s bound and 11 drifted files. The slowest-step criterion is decided; the drift criterion is not: over these three runs 5 files drift in every sample and at most 24 can drift at 5 of 5, which ties the 24 baseline, so close at 5 of 5 if the drift count stays below 24.

Window 7866a48 decided at 5 of 5 (main runs 42449443692 42449766328 42450770597 42451168251 42452530115): node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --since 7866a48 printed slowest Test step p50 15.5 s, target < 18 s: PASS, and drift 11 files over weight by more than 30% (below the 24-file baseline); one shard plan throughout.

Reopened at 0bf0f2e: node scripts/shard-wall-report.mjs --runs 5 prints slowest Test step p50 22.1 s (FAIL); on the #441 plan (--since d81428a, 2 runs) shard p50 14.1-22 s around a mean of 18 s. Summed Test-step seconds per main run grew from 141 s (9c53d7a) to 178-181 s (d81428a, 0bf0f2e) as tests were added, and TEST_FILE_WEIGHTS grew from 426.7 s (7866a48, 42.7 s per shard, PASS at 15.5 s) to 498.9 s (49.9 s per shard): with the mean shard at the target, no rebalance can pass. Cut: 12 shards (41.6 s per shard) and a rule test that holds the summed weight per shard at or below the PASS window's 43 s, so suite growth asks for another shard instead of a FAIL window.

title: Delivery sessions hold a credential that can only propose
body:
Outcome: lead and lane sessions run `git` and `gh` with a GitHub App installation token limited to this repository: contents write, pull requests write, actions write (to re-run a failed job, `src/deliver/gate-wait.ts:138`), checks read, metadata; no workflows, no administration. The token is minted on demand by a git credential helper and a `gh` wrapper, because it expires after one hour; it is not an exported variable. The administrator token stays in the operator's keyring.
Why: every session today can rewrite workflows, rulesets and organization settings (**[R]** V3). This is the one control in section A that rests on exposure alone and needs no incident to justify it. An App is preferred to a fine-grained token because it acts under its own name: it becomes the author of delivery PRs, which A4 needs, and the audit log can tell a lane from the operator [I, to be confirmed by the write tests].
Proof: four write tests with the limited token, each output saved verbatim as a capture (KRN-12): `krn pr ship` end to end including auto-merge; a push that edits a workflow file is refused; `gh api -X PUT` on the ruleset is refused; a token minted after the first has expired works in the same session.
Undo: the launcher falls back to the operator's token behind one flag, set by the operator.
Scope: `scripts/claude/successor-launch.ts`, a minting helper, `docs/program/repository-workflow.md`.
Limit to state in the task: without the sandbox of C1 this protects against a lane that is wrong, not one that is hostile; a session on the host can still ask the keyring for the administrator token. After this slice a commit that edits a workflow file is pushed by the operator's credential; composite actions under `.github/actions/**` are not under the `workflows` permission and stay pushable by the App [I].
Order: A1, A2 and A6 need nobody. A5 needs the operator once. A4 is a choice the operator can decline.
Operator order 2026-11-10: deliver the helper, launcher flag and tests with the App absent; do not create the App or store or mint its key; then give the operator a ten-line instruction (this repository only; contents write, pull requests write, actions write, checks read, metadata; no workflows, no administration).
